notes.text: The chariot — Pharaoh and his chariots and horses, and army. Lay down - In the bottom of the sea. They never rose again to molest the Israelites. Quenched - As the wick of a candle when it is put into the water, is extinguished.

Remember not — Tho' your former deliverance out of Egypt was glorious: yet in comparison of that inestimable mercy of sending the Messiah, all your former deliverances are scarce worthy of your remembrance and consideration.

A new thing — Such a work as was never yet done in the world. Now - The scripture often speaks of things at a great distance of time, as if they were now at hand; to make us sensible of the inconsiderableness of time, and all temporal things, in comparison of God, and eternal things; upon which account it is said, that a thousand years are in God's sight but as one day.
The beast — Shall have cause, if they had abilities, to praise me for their share in this mercy. Dragons - Which live in dry and barren deserts.

glossa.text: *I do new things.* Many things that refresh souls, not bodies: of old I brought forth from the rock one fountain only, to refresh bodies.

*Dragons and ostriches.* The malignant, the venomous, who abode in the solitude of the Gentiles, brutish through the blood of idolatry and the savagery of their manners.

The ostrich has the appearance of wings, but lacks flight. So the hypocrite has the appearance of holiness, but does not have the thing itself.

notes.text: Turned — Brought the captive Israelites out of Babylon into their own land. Dream - We were so surprized and astonished.

Turn — As thou hast brought us home, bring also the rest of our brethren. As - As thou art pleased sometimes to send floods of water into dry and barren grounds, such as the southern parts of Canaan were. We must trust in God for success in all enterprizes, ver. 1, 2. And for children, ver. 3-5. A song of degrees of Solomon.

glossa.text: *A canticle of degrees.* ((CASS.)) The seventh degree, in a figure of the Old Testament, prophesies through Christ who is to come the return from captivity, as it were from Babylon: whence now consolation, and a sowing that more may be reaped. ((AUG.)) Those redeemed by the blood of Christ and turned back from captivity sing these things, while they are pilgrims, groaning by the way. Sion is Jerusalem, eternal in the angels, captive in men. *In the turning.* ((CASS.)) First the greatness of the deed is shown, with the greatness of the joy: secondly he prays for the turning from captivity still to come, there, *Turn again, O Lord. In the turning.* ((AUG.)) Or, when he shall have turned, etc., *as far as turn again, O Lord, our captivity. As.* ((ID.)) It is not always set for a likeness, but for a property, as here; whence it is also said: He did as a just man, which he truly is; so these are made *as men comforted,* that is, they rejoiced, as receiving consolation in the resurrection of Christ, who went before that we might follow.

*Our mouth.* ((CASS.)) The secret of the heart, where joys first are, which afterwards break forth by the office of the tongue. ((AUG.)) *Our mouth.* Of the heart: thence proceeds the evil and the good which cleanses or defiles us; whence not: *That which proceedeth out of the mouth, defileth ((Marc. VII))* . Not of the mouth of the flesh, but of the heart. For thou art not unclean if thou namest thefts and other evils: but while thou thinkest of them, even if thou keep silence. *Among the Gentiles.* ((ID.)) Not the Gentiles, because not all believe. *He hath magnified,* because they see them work miracles also; a firm testimony from an adversary. ((CASS.)) And he has truly magnified, lest thou doubt because of the words of the Gentiles.

*Turn again, O Lord.* ((ID.)) The second part. He prays for the turning which is to come, in which there shall be a sowing in hope of joy. ((ID.)) The redemption of the coming of the Lord having been foretold, they pray again that their own sins be forgiven. In the general remission they rejoice, and they pray pardon for themselves. *Turn again, O Lord, our captivity.* ((ID.)) There was none according to the letter in the days of David, but under the devil the world was captive, etc., *as far as* it is not therefore to be given over, because *he that soweth in tears.* ((THEOD.)) He calls Jerusalem the south, etc., *as far as* that they may be constrained, and make their way after the manner of a torrent.

*In tears.* ((AUG.)) Spiritual sowing is always in tears, whence: *Blessed are they that mourn.* But they who sow in the flesh, sow with gladness: but afterwards weeping: because *mourning taketh hold of the end of joy.* ((ID.)) Zacchaeus, *Behold the half,* etc., *as far as: He that shall give a cup of cold water shall not lose his reward ((Matth. X))*.

*Going.* ((CASS.)) By the advancement of a better life. *Casting,* sending on before them into that world. *Their own,* not of rapine, but of their own labour; *coming,* to the judgment. This is common to all, but to joy none come but the good. *And they wept.* ((AUG.)) Because they were wretched, etc., *as far as* he wishes that many be sick.

notes.text: Though I — He subjoins this in the singular number, because the Philippians could not say thus.

Circumcised the eighth day — Not at ripe age, as a proselyte. Of the tribe of Benjamin - Sprung from the wife, not the handmaid. An Hebrew of Hebrews - By both my parents; in everything, nation, religion, language. Touching the law, a pharisee - One of that sect who most accurately observe it.
Having such a zeal for it as to persecute to the death those who did not observe it. Touching the righteousness which is described and enjoined by the Law — That is, external observances, blameless.
But all these things, which I then accounted gain, which were once my confidence, my glory, and joy, those, ever since I have believed, I have accounted loss, nothing worth in comparison of Christ.

Yea, I still account both all these and all things else to be mere loss, compared to the inward, experimental knowledge of Christ, as my Lord, as my prophet, priest, and king, as teaching me wisdom, atoning for my sins, and reigning in my heart. To refer this to justification only, is miserably to pervert the whole scope of the words. They manifestly relate to sanctification also; yea, to that chiefly. For whom I have actually suffered the loss of all things — Which the world loves, esteems, or admires; of which I am so far from repenting, that I still account them but dung - The discourse rises. Loss is sustained with patience, but dung is cast away with abhorrence. The Greek word signifies any, the vilest refuse of things, the dross of metals, the dregs of liquors, the excrements of animals, the most worthless scraps of meat, the basest offals, fit only for dogs. That I may gain Christ - He that loses all things, not excepting himself, gains Christ, and is gained by Christ. And still there is more; which even St. Paul speaks of his having not yet gained.

And be found by God ingrafted in him, not having my own righteousness, which is of the law — That merely outward righteousness prescribed by the law, and performed by my own strength. But that inward righteousness which is through faith - Which can flow from no other fountain. The righteousness which is from God - From his almighty Spirit, not by my own strength, but by faith alone. Here also the apostle is far from speaking of justification only.

The knowledge of Christ, mentioned in the eighth verse, is here more largely explained. That I may know him — As my complete saviour. And the power of his resurrection - Raising me from the death of sin, into all the life of love. And the fellowship of his sufferings - Being crucified with him. And made conformable to his death - So as to be dead to all things here below.
The resurrection of the dead — That is, the resurrection to glory.

Not that I have already attained — The prize. He here enters on a new set of metaphors, taken from a race. But observe how, in the utmost fervour, he retains his sobriety of spirit. Or am already perfected - There is a difference between one that is perfect, and one that is perfected. The one is fitted for the race, ver. 15; the other, ready to receive the prize. But I pursue, if I may apprehend that - Perfect holiness, preparatory to glory. For, in order to which I was apprehended by Christ Jesus - Appearing to me in the way, Acts xxvi, 14. The speaking conditionally both here and in the preceding verse, implies no uncertainty, but only the difficulty of attaining.
I do not account myself to have apprehended this already; to be already possessed of perfect holiness.

Forgetting the things that are behind — Even that part of the race which is already run. And reaching forth unto - Literally, stretched out over the things that are before - Pursuing with the whole bent and vigour of my soul, perfect holiness and eternal glory. In Christ Jesus - The author and finisher of every good thing.

glossa.text: *Although I also,* etc. Lest the Apostle should seem to despise in others what he himself does not have, and not to be able to trust in the flesh, he subjoins: *Although,* etc.

*Of the tribe of Benjamin.* The tribe of Benjamin clave to Judah, not departing from the temple, when the separation was made under the servant of Solomon. For then the tribe of Judah, which was royal, and the tribe of Benjamin, and the tribe of Levi, which was priestly, remained together, not departing from Jerusalem and from the temple.
*For Christ.* Lest I should show the coming of Christ either not yet accomplished, or to be superfluous. For all these hindrances were empty things, that one might not come to grace.

*Nevertheless I esteem.* Not only for the sake of having Christ have I so judged, but even if I could not attain him. *For* this alone, namely for the *knowledge* which we have of Jesus, *pre-eminent,* above the other kinds of knowledge. *As dung.* As if: Not only the losses of goods, but the things which defile one who is now observing them: and this to this end, that in the future they may have Christ for their reward: and that here I may be a member in him: which cannot come about otherwise unless I esteem those things as dung.

*My own righteousness,* etc. If righteousness is from the law, how is it thine? Didst thou impose the law upon thyself? God gave the law and imposed it. God commanded thee to obey his law. But it is also thine, because thou presumest upon the law, reckoning that by thine own will thou canst fulfil the law.

((CHRYS.)) Rightly did he say: *Not having my own righteousness,* etc., *as far as* which have proceeded from our own zeal.

*But that,* etc. ((AUG.)) Which obtains from God, which takes away fear, etc., *as far as* it is wholly to be taken away according to the shadow of the figures of the law. *Righteousness in faith.* That is, righteousness is a thing existing in faith, and as it was born of faith, so it has no being save in faith.

*Unto the knowing.* He subjoins the commendation of faith, by the many things which it does. For it makes us know God perfectly in the other life also, who here is believed. And to have the resurrection, which our resurrection is the power and efficacy of the resurrection of Christ And in this life to have fellowship in suffering: for unless through faith, no man would suffer so great things; and the conformation of [his] death, that is, that we may die, as he did, if there be need.

*I may meet.* Rendering to God the things which he has bestowed on me, and by this coming to the resurrection. Or, I may meet Christ in the judgment, which belongs to the saints only, coming first to the true and glorious resurrection, which is not among the dead, but far out of the dead: because, although all rise again on the day of judgment, yet the just alone shall be gloriously changed, and shall meet the Lord in the air, borne up by angels. But the ungodly shall remain on the earth until they receive the terrible sentence of the judge.

*Not that I have already received.* This he says of himself, lest those whom he praises should be exalted as men, but should add labour, as he himself does who is so great. *But I follow after,* etc. Not with the steps of the body, but with the affections of the mind and the manners of life, that I may be able to be a perfect possessor of righteousness: I who, advancing by a straight road from day to day by spiritual renewal, am already a perfect wayfarer of that same righteousness. For he was a perfect wayfarer, but not yet one arrived by the perfection of the journey itself. *If by any means I may comprehend.* This he says because it is difficult. And lest it should seem superfluous to suffer so many things, since he has faith and the other good things, he subjoins: Deservedly do I labour so much for that glory, because I do *Not* say that I have *already received* anything: for if I have received anything of glory, it is nothing in comparison with what is to come. *Or* if I have received anything, as concerning the knowledge of Christ, I do not say that in it *I am perfect.* And if it is thus of me. what of me who of others?
*The things which are behind.* His former deeds, not because they were evil, but small toward merit, but stretched out toward the better things, that he may always advance unto what is better.
*I press on.* Even so far, until I come to the appointed good. *Of the supernal vocation.* That is, of eternal life, unto which God calls, and therefore it is a worthy thing, etc.

notes.text: Six days before the passover — Namely, on the Sabbath: that which was called by the Jews, "The Great Sabbath." This whole week was anciently termed "The great and holy week." Jesus came - From Ephraim, chap. xi, 54.

It seems Martha was a person of some figure, from the great respect which was paid to her and her sister, in visits and condolences on Lazarus' death, as well as from the costly ointment mentioned in the next verse. And probably it was at their house our Lord and his disciples lodged, when he returned from Jerusalem to Bethany, every evening of the last week of his life, upon which he was now entered.

Then Mary, taking a pound of ointment — There were two persons who poured ointment on Christ. One toward the beginning of his ministry, at or near Nain, Luke vii, 37, &c. The other six days before his last passover, at Bethany; the account of whom is given here, as well as by St. Matthew and Mark.
Against the day of my burial — Which now draws nigh.

glossa.text: *He came into Bethania.* Therefore he came first to Bethania, that the raising of Lazarus might be handed down more deeply to the memory of all, and that the Jews might be confounded as inexcusable, plotting the death of so great a raiser of the dead.

*Mary therefore.* Precious ointment is made of nard, chiefly of the spikes; but here it is called pistic from the place whence it came. And it is interpreted "faithful," not corrupted by any other admixture. *Then said one.* Judas, although evil, is nevertheless numbered among the apostles, that we may be taught to bear with the evil, lest we divide the body of Christ, and that the evil do not harm the good.

*Not because,* etc. As far as his own intention went, it did not pertain to him concerning the needy, because he did not care for them; not because it had been committed to him to dispense to the poor.

*Having the purse,* etc. He to whom the angels minister has purses for the expenses of the poor, condescending to the weak.

*Let her alone.* He knows the thief, but does not betray him, teaching us to bear with the evil. He commends so great a service of Mary, showing that he was to die and to be anointed with spices for burial. Therefore to Mary, to whom it was not permitted to anoint him dead, it was given to bestow the office of a funeral upon him living; whence according to Mark it is said that what she had, that is, what she could, this she did, *she is come beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.*

*But me you have not always.* By bodily presence. Or you shall not have me, thou Judas and those who are of this sort, because if the evil now communicate in the sacraments, yet afterwards they do not have the Lord as the good do.

registers.label: Spare
lines: God is doing a new thing; do you not perceive it?
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
A way through the wilderness, rivers in the desert.
We press on toward the prize of God's call.
Mary breaks the jar; the house fills with the scent of love.
We pour out our lives; come, let us worship.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Breathe in — the whole house fills with the scent of broken nard, a year's wages poured out over his feet.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
She loosens her hair and wipes his feet, and the fragrance follows him toward the tomb he will not refuse.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
For God is making a way in the wilderness, rivers where the ground was only dust.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy. Press on; the road bends now toward Jerusalem.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Mary pours the costly nard, and the house is filled with its fragrance.
Turn us, O God, and we will return.
God is making a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert.
Turn us, O God, and we will return.
We press on toward the goal; the road turns to Jerusalem.
Turn us, O God, and we will return. Amen.
